titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 9/2014 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޤާނޫނުލްޢުޤޫބާތު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Maldives Penal Code (Law No. 9/2014). It makes gambling and running a gambling place, including online, a crime, graded as a Class 4 felony. It rewrites the offence of receiving stolen property so it also covers laundering, selling, importing, exporting and trading stolen goods, including online. It also rewrites the forgery article to cover counterfeiting and passing off fake items as genuine, with a wider definition of 'document' that includes electronic records, money and intellectual property.
whyItMatters: Placing a bet or running a betting business, in person or online, could lead to a felony conviction. Selling, moving or dealing in goods known to be stolen, and faking documents or items, would carry clearer and in some cases heavier grades.
keyProvisions: Article 218 is renamed to cover receiving and trafficking stolen property. Taking, holding or keeping someone else's property without checking whether it is stolen, and not to return it to the owner, stays an offence, graded one level below theft under Article 210(b).

New parts of Article 218 make it an offence to transfer stolen property to someone else, disguise its origin or ownership, or knowingly hide it. Knowingly selling, importing or exporting, distributing or supplying stolen goods, or dealing in them online, is also an offence. These are graded one level above theft under Article 210(b).

The chapter and Article 310 headings change to cover forgery, counterfeiting and fraudulent acts. Article 310 makes it an offence to create or alter a document, or an item falsely shown as made by a certain person, original, valuable or antique, with intent to cause harm or hide wrongdoing, or to knowingly rely on such a fake.

Article 310 defines 'document' widely: printed or electronic records, money (coins and notes), stamps, seals, badges and tokens, electronic signatures and registry data, and intellectual property such as trademarks and copyright.

Forgery of a document that creates or affects legal rights, or is issued by or to the government, is a Class 4 felony. Forging money, bonds, stocks, securities or financial instruments is a Class 3 felony. Other cases are a Class 5 felony.

Article 616 (on not fasting in Ramadan, drinking alcohol and sorcery) adds gambling to its heading and makes gambling and running a gambling place a Class 4 felony. 'Gambling' means staking something of value on the outcome of a game, sport or event. Free-entry contests, free prize draws and amusement machines that give only free plays or tokens are excluded. The law would take effect when published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: People who gamble or run betting businesses or online betting, people who buy, sell or trade second-hand goods, and anyone accused of forgery or counterfeiting.
statedReasons: The government says the bill makes gambling and running gambling places a crime, and changes the elements and grades of some existing Penal Code offences.
